question: Can a reusable hierarchical graph grammar induced without role labels compress frozen critical-edge graphs better than a flat local dictionary, and do its learned derivations remain more conserved when structural role is preserved than when role is broken?

rationaleParentV7.resultUsedAsRationaleOnly: radius-2 length-aware local wiring neighborhoods were the only predeclared primary representation to clear the Cleveland evidence gate and they transferred to Bavaria; V7 did not establish that normalized length itself was the causal ingredient
rationaleParentV7.purpose: V7 justifies testing whether the graph contains reusable compositional structure, but V8 deliberately refuses V7's radius boundary and asks the compressor to discover reusable connected units by description-length reduction.

primitiveGraph.observationsForInduction: all unique V5 pair-eligible observations whose frozen lane is train
nodeLabel: full frozen critical-center degree class capped at 6+
frozen self-loop multiplicity class capped at 3+
primitiveGraph.parallelPaths: all literal parallel non-self center-to-center paths are collapsed to one undirected primitive edge
primitiveGraph.primaryEdgeLabel: parallel multiplicity class plus mean observation-diagonal-normalized path-step bin of width 0.05

grammarFamily.name: lossless binary edge-bundle contraction grammar
grammarFamily.nonterminalRule: a binary rule X -> A + B + the complete bundle of residual edges internal to A/B, including each internal edge label and the port path into each child
grammarFamily.portPath: a binary child-address path; external residual edges retain exact attachment by prefixing 0 for the left child or 1 for the right child when a contraction occurs
grammarFamily.losslessness: expanding every nonterminal and replaying residual edges reconstructs the identity-free primitive graph exactly
grammarFamily.candidate: any adjacent current supernode pair together with the complete current internal edge bundle between them
grammarFamily.candidateIdentity: child symbols plus canonical internal-edge bundle; external context is not part of the rule identity
grammarFamily.orientation: canonical child-symbol order; unresolved automorphism-equivalent ties may use an ephemeral observation-local ordinal only to choose a representative contraction, never as a rule feature or score
grammarFamily.selection: within the frozen top-32 shortlist, choose the candidate with the largest exact positive description-length reduction; ties prefer greater distinct-source support, then greater selected occurrence count, then canonical candidate hash
grammarFamily.application: contract a deterministic maximal non-overlapping set of the selected rule in every induction graph
grammarFamily.stop: stop when no shortlisted candidate with the minimum support yields a strictly positive exact description-length reduction, or when maxRules/maxDerivationDepth is reached

descriptionCode.unit: bits under a fixed explicit structural code; this is the experiment's MDL code and is not claimed to be an optimal universal graph code
descriptionCode.integer: Elias-gamma length; zero-valued counts are encoded as gamma(value+1)
descriptionCode.symbolReference: gamma(symbolId+1); terminal symbol IDs are lexicographic and nonterminal IDs are induction order
descriptionCode.edgeLabelReference: gamma(edgeLabelId+1) with lexicographically frozen edge-label IDs
descriptionCode.residualEdgeEndpoints: two fixed 32-bit observation-local node references so description length is invariant to node renumbering
descriptionCode.residualEdge: two endpoint references + edge-label reference + both port-path codes
descriptionCode.portPathCode: gamma(pathLength+1) plus one raw bit per path step
descriptionCode.grammarModel: gamma(ruleCount+1) plus, for each rule in induction order, both child-symbol references, gamma(internalEdgeCount+1), and the exact internal-edge label/port-path records
descriptionCode.trainingTotal: grammar model bits + encoded Cleveland induction graphs
descriptionCode.heldoutData: encoded heldout graphs under the frozen grammar; model bits are reported separately and are not recharged per heldout lane

models.raw: no learned rules; primitive graph encoded directly
models.flat: same greedy coding and support rules, but every rule must have two terminal children; nonterminals may never appear on a rule right-hand side
models.hierarchical: full grammarFamily; previously induced nonterminals may appear as rule children
models.topologyAblation: repeat raw/flat/hierarchical induction with topology-only edge labels; this is a required ablation, not a second discovery representation

frozenGrammarEvaluation.applicationToNewGraph: start from primitive terminals and replay frozen rules in induction order, contracting a deterministic maximal non-overlapping set of exact rule matches; rules are never refit or reordered
recordPerObservation: for every original center, ordered ancestry of nonterminal rule IDs from leaf outward

heldoutCompressionClaim.condition1: hierarchical heldout data bits are strictly lower than flat heldout data bits in aggregate
heldoutCompressionClaim.condition2: hierarchical beats flat within at least 60% of distinct holdout sourceGroupIds
heldoutCompressionClaim.condition3: hierarchical training total bits including its model are strictly lower than flat training total bits including its model
heldoutCompressionClaim.interpretation: all three are required to claim that recursive composition adds compressive structure beyond a flat dictionary

frozenGrammarEvaluation.controlInterpretation: LOC compression is reported without requiring failure; cross-world compression may reflect genuinely shared structure and is not by itself a role claim

roleSpecificity.labelsOpenedOnlyAfter: both length-aware grammars and the topology ablation grammars are frozen and hashed
roleSpecificity.centerCorrespondence: reproduce the frozen V4/V5 D4-aligned sparse critical-center correspondence with 8 nearest candidates per center kind; grammar induction never sees this mapping
roleSpecificity.centerMetric: normalized Levenshtein distance between the two mapped centers' hierarchical rule-ancestry sequences, with insertion/deletion/substitution cost 1 and denominator max(1, lenA, lenB)
roleSpecificity.pairMetric: mean mapped-center ancestry distance within an observation pair
roleSpecificity.flatControlMetric: the identical ancestry-distance calculation under the frozen flat grammar
roleSpecificity.effect: family-pair-balanced smaller-is-more-conserved rank effect; positive means grammar derivations mutate less in role-preserving pairs
roleSpecificity.nullShuffle: shuffle preserved/broken observation-pair labels within exact physical-family pair while preserving the original preserved count
roleSpecificity.hierarchicalRoleClaim: requires the hierarchical primary pair metric to meet the Cleveland evidence gate and the Bavaria holdout magnitude gate
roleSpecificity.hierarchyAddsRoleInformation: reported descriptively as hierarchical balanced effect minus flat balanced effect; no separate claim threshold is imposed because the primary hierarchy claim already requires heldout compression superiority over flat

adjudication.hierarchicalGrammar: If recursive grammar beats flat on all three heldoutCompressionClaim conditions and its hierarchical ancestry mutation meets Cleveland + Bavaria role gates, treat the graph as supporting a reusable hierarchical generative architecture whose learned productions track preserved structural role.
adjudication.compressionOnly: If recursive grammar beats flat in heldout compression but ancestry mutation fails the role gate, conclude that reusable hierarchy exists but this experiment has not tied that hierarchy to the preserved-role distinction.
adjudication.roleWithoutHierarchy: If ancestry mutation passes but recursive heldout compression does not beat flat, do not call the result hierarchical grammar; treat it as another local correspondence signal and stop the compression claim.
adjudication.flatSuffices: If flat matches or beats hierarchical heldout compression, reusable local pieces are sufficient under this compressor and recursive composition is not supported.
adjudication.noCompression: If neither learned model lowers Cleveland total description length relative to raw, reject this grammar family rather than tuning after the result.
adjudication.topologyAblation: If topology-only reaches the same adjudication as length-aware, normalized path length is not required for the compression grammar; if only length-aware succeeds, carry length-aware forward but do not call length causal without a separate intervention test.

falsifiers.parentDrift: abort if frozen V5 manifest/world/projector/role-row hashes differ from the expected packet
falsifiers.labelLeakage: abort if preserved/broken role labels are read before grammar packets are written and hashed
falsifiers.nonLosslessRule: abort if synthetic expand(contract(graph)) round-trip checks fail for any rule case including external attachments, multiple internal edges, or nested nonterminals
falsifiers.insufficientPairSupport: abort role claim if fewer than 50 Cleveland eligible pairs retain at least one mapped center with a derivation metric
falsifiers.heldoutCollapse: no hierarchical grammar claim if Bavaria aggregate recursive compression does not beat flat or if fewer than 60% of Bavaria source groups improve
falsifiers.flatParity: no recursive claim if flat training total bits are <= hierarchical training total bits or flat heldout data bits are <= hierarchical
falsifiers.roleTransferCollapse: no role-linked grammar claim if Cleveland passes but Bavaria ancestry effect reverses or falls below +0.08
